newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Ousted Afghan government forces attack Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Afghan government forces attack Taleban.

text.p: Forces loyal to the ousted Afghan government launched a blistering assault on Taleban troops on Thursday north of the capital Kabul.
Fierce artillery and rocket duels churned up columns of dust around the strategic De Sabz pass, 30 km (20 miles) north of Kabul, Reuters correspondent Chris Bird reported.
"God willing we will take the pass today," said Niq Mohammad, a commander with the ousted government forces under military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
He said the attack, a pincer-movement to support forces belonging to northern Uzbek leader chief Abdul Rashid Dostum, began around 6 am (0130 gmt).
He said the anti-Taleban alliance had gained some ground but there was no way of independently confirming this.

He said Taleban heavy weapons were firing on their positions from the other side of the mountains. Several shells and rockets were landing each minute. Deafening crashes and flashes signalled Taleban rockets hitting positions held by ousted government troops.
